subject: Re: ACME - Rerank model exploration / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Rerank model exploration / next steps

Hi Jenna / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — good to meet and walk through your reranking use case and constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

1) What we heard from you
- Primary goal: improve ranking relevance for product search (homepage + category pages) where current NDCG@10 ~0.48 and MRR ~0.34 for the latest benchmark (see Jenna's follow-up).
- Latency requirement: p95 generation + rerank < 220ms for the combined flow.
- Throughput: ~400 requests/minute during peak.
- Data: you can share a representative sample of 50k queries & relevance judgments (we only need de-identified IDs + label columns).

2) Our immediate proposed plan
- Step A (evaluation): run offline rerank experiments using your benchmark (NDCG@10 / MRR / click-through regression checks) across 3 candidate model variants and baseline. We’ll return NDCG/MRR CSV + per-query breakdown.
- Step B (A/B plan): small live A/B canary (2% traffic -> 10% over 2 weeks) with close monitoring on click-through and NDCG proxy.
- Step C (rollout): canary-to-grade rollout if no negative quality regressions.

3) Deliverables and timing
- I’ll kick off offline runs as soon as we get: (a) the benchmark file (50k sample), (b) example prompt sets / templates for reranker scoring.
- Expect first offline results (NDCG/MRR CSV + short write-up) within 4 business days after we get the data.

4) Risks / checks
- We’ll include a regression-alert rule on NDCG@10 drop > 0.02 absolute and MRR drop > 0.015 absolute; if triggered we’ll pause A/B.

Attached: prompt-sets-v1.xlsx (template) — please fill in the example prompts and label mapping.

Next steps: Jenna — can you share the benchmark CSV + confirm an internal owner for sample delivery? Also confirm whether you want us to run both re-ranking-only and hybrid (generate+rerank) variants.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: prompt-sets-v1.xlsx (Excel, 28KB)

From: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>

Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Rerank model exploration / next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below and I attached the benchmark slice.

- Benchmark snapshot: attached acme-bench-20260714.csv (50,012 queries, relevance labels 0-3). Current offline baseline numbers: NDCG@10 = 0.48, MRR = 0.34 (these are computed on our holdout).
- Example prompts: we have a standard scoring prompt (column in the CSV) — I filled the template where possible.
- Hybrid vs rerank-only: we prefer rerank-only first to isolate model impact; if results look promising we’ll test hybrid in a later phase.

A couple of asks: 
1) Can you share which candidate models you’ll evaluate?
2) Can you include per-segment metrics (search vs category) since category pages are higher priority?

Link to full benchmark + labels (internal Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AexampleAcmeBench

Attached: acme-bench-20260714.csv

Thanks,
Jenna
Senior Search PM — Acme Corp

Attachment: acme-bench-20260714.csv (CSV, 6.8MB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Rerank model exploration / next steps

Hi Jenna —

Got the benchmark — thanks for the fast turnaround. Below is the plan and the candidate models we’ll run in the offline eval. We’ll produce NDCG@10, MRR, and per-query delta vs your baseline, plus per-segment (search vs category).

Candidate variants:
- baseline: your current production scoring (vector + lexical mix)
- redwood-rerank-v1 (dense reranker, 125M) — quick, low-latency baseline to set expectations
- redwood-rerank-v2 (transformer reranker, 1.3B, optimized kernels, recommended first-run)
- laion-rerank-7b-quant (7B quantized variant) — for a higher-quality / cost tradeoff check

Evaluation plan:
- Offline runs: full 50k sample against all variants. Output: per-query scores, NDCG@k (k=1,3,5,10), MRR, precision@1, and latency distribution for scoring step.
- Regression checks: compare to your baseline; we’ll flag any absolute NDCG@10 drop > 0.02 or relative drop > 4%.
- A/B proposal: if redwood-rerank-v2 shows >= 0.02 absolute NDCG uplift (or MRR uplift >= 0.015) on offline, we propose a 2% -> 10% two-week canary (monitor: CTR, NDCG proxy, latency, error rate).

Links / attachments:
- Internal eval run (will publish results here when ready): https://redwood-internal.company/evals/acme-rerank-dashboard?run=2026-07-15
- Attached: prompt-sets-v1.xlsx (I filled a couple of alternate prompt templates for the reranker).

Time estimate: first offline results by EOD Monday (4 business days from receipt). I’ll include the CSV with NDCG/MRR breakdown and a short summary.

Note on quality regression concerns: we’ll also run a per-query stability check — if high-traffic queries flip frequently in the top-3, that’s a signal we should tune prompts/temperature or fall back to the baseline for that query bucket.

If this looks good I’ll kick off the job now.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: prompt-sets-v1.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)

Jenna — looping in commercial so we can align on POC terms and timeline.

- POC A: 2-week canary using Redwood hosted inference (no infra changes) — standard usage billing, quick to spin up.
- POC B: Dedicated reserved pool for predictable latency (monthly commit) — recommended if you plan to scale beyond testing.

Quick Qs:

Marissa / Aditya —

Thanks for the plan and options. We’re ready to proceed with the offline eval and want to target the live canary to start the week of Aug 3rd. A few confirmations:

- Targets for canary: aim for >= +0.02 absolute NDCG@10 uplift (vs baseline 0.48) OR >= +0.015 MRR uplift. If neither threshold is met, we’ll not graduate to live traffic.
- Canary traffic: start 2% for 3 days, evaluate, then ramp to 10% for 11 days if metrics look stable.
- Latency SLO: p95 combined flow <= 220ms. If we breach latency SLO by > 10% we’ll pause.

Please proceed with the offline runs and share the NDCG/MRR CSV when ready. Once we have the offline uplift numbers and latency profile we’ll confirm the Aug 3 start and contract POC terms (procurement is CC'd).

On a related note, I’d appreciate a per-segment breakdown (search vs category) in the results.

Thanks,
Tom Ellis
Head of Search — Acme Corp
